neighbours.label: the head noun that completes a two-word compound or place name: ' cell' / ' cells' after its modifier (nerve cell), ' Island' / ' Canyon' after the proper name (Pine Island, Glen Canyon); the bare noun stays quiet
fire: Researchers grew a single muscle cell in a dish for three weeks.
Our ferry reached Vancouver Island just before sunset.
We spent two days hiking through Bryce Canyon in the rain.
The therapy replaces damaged stem cells in the bone marrow.
Her grandparents arrived at Ellis Island with one suitcase.
A hydrogen fuel cell powers the bus on this route.
The road winds down into Antelope Canyon past red cliffs.
Tourists love the beaches of Kangaroo Island in spring.
quiet: Researchers kept the cell in a dish for three weeks.
Our ferry reached the island just before sunset.
We spent two days hiking through the canyon in the rain.
The therapy replaces the cells that were damaged in the marrow.
Her grandparents arrived on the island with one suitcase.
This cell powers the bus on this route.
The road winds down into the canyon past red cliffs.
Tourists love the beaches of this island in spring.

short: compound head: X cell, X Island
notes: Probes: 'nerve cell' 0.75, 'Pine Island' 0.67, 'Glen Canyon' 0.73, 'socketserver' 0.79; 'The cell was' 0.02, 'The island was' 0.03; sentence-initial 'Blood cells' only 0.12, and 'customer service' 0.01, so not every compound fires. Fire items use compounds that were not in the top examples.
